rationale: Evidence from iteration 5 (score 712.7, best so far): oval (951.8) and s-bend (944.8) both finish 20/20, but slalom finishes 0/20 (off-track 20, progress 0.58, max_error 0.061, about 1 line-loss event per run). The slalom is the entire remaining gap. Iterations 2 to 5 show that the sensor footprint (0.016) and extra kd (1.0 to 1.3) each gave small gains on slalom progress (0.36 to 0.55 to 0.58) without hurting the other tracks. Those levers appear to be saturating. The slalom's failure is a lag problem: the sensors sit 0.05 m ahead of the axle, so the controller reacts only after the robot has drifted to the 0.06 m limit on each alternating bend. Change 1: move all five sensors forward from y = 0.05 to y = 0.07, giving about 2 cm more look-ahead so steering starts earlier on tight alternations. The x layout and weights are unchanged, so the signal scale is preserved. Change 2: raise kd from 1.3 to 1.5 to damp the faster signal changes that the earlier sensing produces. kp 2.0, ki 0, base_speed 1.0, wheel_track 0.11, last_direction line loss and the rest of the geometry are unchanged, so oval and s-bend should stay near their current finish rates. Risk: the look-ahead gain may over-steer on the s-bend (control effort was 5.3 at iteration 5). If s-bend control effort rises above 6.5, or oscillation rises above 0.3, the next step is to revert the sensor y to 0.05 and keep kd at 1.5. Expected result: slalom progress above 0.7, slalom max_error below 0.055, and a chance of the first slalom finishes. Hypotheses: H1, slalom off-track exits are caused by late reaction to the tape, which the forward sensors should reduce. H2, the extra kd damps the overshoot that the earlier sensing introduces. Next measurements: per-track progress, max_error, line_loss_events and completion_time on slalom (to check the 3 s limit at base_speed 1.0), and control_effort and steering_oscillation on s-bend to test for over-steering.
